findings.text: follow-on: _manifest_write_paths scans the delivered manifest with line.startswith(key + ':') for orientation_write_paths and changed_paths, re-implementing the field reader this module already owns at _manifest_field_lines (reckon/crew/review.py:1756), whose docstring states it stays local on purpose so the read path cannot fail a review on a field it does not know. The new scan is the weaker of the two: it misses an indented key line and the empty-value block form that _MANIFEST_FIELD_RE and _manifest_field_lines handle, so a manifest whose orientation_write_paths is written beneath its key as a block reads as no declared paths and the fallback silently yields nothing.

follow-on: project_declares_review_checks re-resolves the domain block itself (flight.resolve, resolved.config.get('domain'), DomainConfig.model_validate) rather than asking the owner of that read, reckon/crew/domain_rules.py:106 rules_for, whose module docstring states it 'is the one place that answers which of those rules a node touches, so the brief a node is dispatched with, the review it receives and the checks run at promotion all read the same match rather than composing their own'. The node-less question it answers is not owned elsewhere, but the block-resolution preamble is now spelled twice and can drift from rules_for.

follow-on: the bullet added by a9934a9b3 states 'eight caused by the cut, across test_a_figure_review_promotes_without_text_scores.py and test_review_record_contract.py', but the sweep it cites (smoke-after.log) shows seven of those eight in those two files and the eighth in tests/test_a_review_answers_the_domain_checks.py::test_a_record_with_no_readable_reviewed_run_owes_nothing, the node's own test the repair replaces; the cited file set is one short of the count it is offered as the source of, and the 'seed records naming runs they never create' clause does not describe the eighth.

follow-on: the fragment cites 're-running them together with this node's own file gives 29 passed' and the manifest's artifacts line records the same figure, but no log for that run is written under the run directory: the only receipt is a tool result in the run's transcript ('29 passed in 17.27s'), so a reader reconciling the fragment against the logs it is the record of finds no file for the measurement it quotes.
